Skills for AI

InsightPage extended Markdown syntax rules, DSL specifications, and examples tailored for AI assistants and LLMs.

InsightPage Markdown Syntax

Use these extensions in addition to standard Markdown and Mermaid.

Use different fence lengths for nested code fences.

Tabs

Use tabs for switchable sections. Start each tab with --- <Tab Title>.

```tabs
--- Overview
Summary...
--- Details
Specifications...
```

Map

InsightPage supports interactive maps rendered using Leaflet.js via map or leaflet code blocks.

1. Interactive Map Example

```map
center:
  lat: 51.505
  lng: -0.09
zoom: 13
height: 380px
markers:
  - lat: 51.505
    lng: -0.09
    title: "Central London"
    popup: "<b>Central London</b><br>Heart of the city."
    color: "#ef4444"
  - lat: 51.515
    lng: -0.1
    title: "British Museum"
    popup: "<b>British Museum</b><br>World-famous history and culture museum."
    color: "#3b82f6"
  - lat: 51.5007
    lng: -0.1246
    title: "Big Ben"
    popup: "<b>Big Ben & Houses of Parliament</b>"
    color: "#10b981"
lines:
  - coordinates:
      - [51.505, -0.09]
      - [51.515, -0.1]
      - [51.5007, -0.1246]
      - [51.505, -0.09]
    color: "#8b5cf6"
```

2. Configuration Reference

Use YAML or JSON inside a map block:

  • center: Map center coordinates as { lat, lng } or [lat, lng].
  • zoom: Initial zoom level (integer from 1 to 19, default 13).
  • height / width: Map container dimensions (e.g., 380px, 100%).
  • markers: List of marker objects or [lat, lng, popup] tuples.
    • lat, lng: Coordinates.
    • title: Tooltip text.
    • popup: HTML / text displayed on click.
    • color: Pin accent color (e.g., #ef4444, #3b82f6).
  • lines / polylines: Array of lines with coordinates and color options.
  • polygons: Polygon shapes with coordinates, fillColor, and stroke color.
  • circles: Circle overlays with lat, lng, radius (in meters), and popup.
  • geojson: Raw GeoJSON object or string to plot vector geographic layers.

Timeline Charts

Use timeline code blocks for zoomable, interactive timelines with adaptive time axes, horizontal panning, collection tags, and automatic categorical color discovery.

Supported Syntaxes & Formats

  • Standard YAML/JSON array of events: [{start, end, title, ...}] or list - start: ...
  • Loose Double-Brace Object: {{start: 2020-01-01, title: Project Alpha, end: 2021-06-01}}
  • External Dataset Files & Schema Mapping: data: path/to/file.csv with schemas: { title, start, end, collection, categories } (requires granting a local folder as FS Vault, or using absolute http(s):// / data: URLs)
  • Markdown Table Sourcing: table: "#table-id" or id: my-table linking directly to note tables (works directly without file system permissions)

Event Fields & Configuration

  • start: ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD), timestamp, or BC/negative year number (e.g. -3000-08-01, 3000 BC, -2400).
  • end: End date or year (optional; omitted or Date.now() extends to present day). Using Date.now() renders the vertical “Today” indicator line.
  • title: Event title label displayed above or on the event bar. Supports wikilinks ([[Note Title]]).
  • collection: Array of related project or publication tags ([Tag1, Tag2]). Collapses into +N badges on tight zoom.
  • [customCategory]: Any custom key (e.g., type, institution, category, region) is automatically discovered, colored, and mapped to interactive category selection controls.
```timeline
- start: 2020-01-01
  end: 2021-06-30
  title: Research Phase
  category: R&D
  collection: [Survey, Paper]

- start: 2021-07-01
  end: Date.now()
  title: Product Rollout
  category: Operations
  collection: [V1, V2]
```

Charts (Chart DSL)

Use chart with YAML configuration for interactive charts rendered via Observable Plot and D3.

Unified Chart Configuration Reference

All Chart DSL charts share a consistent set of configuration keys:

Category Options & Syntax Description Supported Chart Types
Chart Types type: bar | line | pie | donut (doughnut) | polararea | radar | sankey | scatter (point, scatterplot) Specify the visualization type to render. All Chart Types
Data Sourcing id: table-id / table: "#table-id"
data: path/to/file.csv
source: / file: / dataset:		 Bind directly to markdown tables (with or without # / ^ prefixes) or external CSV / TSV / JSON data files. All Chart Types
Mark Lines markLines: / markLine: / marks:
- { y: 80, label: "Target", style: dashed, color: "#10b981", strokeWidth: 1.5 }
- { x: 50, label: "Threshold", style: dotted }
- { x: "Q3", label: "Milestone" }		 Add horizontal (y:) or vertical (x:) reference threshold lines with labels and custom styling (solid, dashed, dotted). Supports both numeric and categorical coordinates. Bar, Line, Scatter
Scales & Log Scales xScale: log / yScale: log
xLog: true / yLog: true
scales: { x: { type: log }, y: { type: log } }		 Switch axis scale to logarithmic. Automatically suppresses 0-baseline collision on log scales. Bar, Line, Scatter
Domain & Min/Max xMin: 0 / xMax: 100
yMin: 0 / yMax: 500
xDomain: [0, 50] / yDomain: [100, 1000]		 Pin explicit bounds and intervals for X or Y axes. Bar, Line, Scatter
Axis Inversion & Visibility xReverse: true / yReverse: true
xDisplay: false / yDisplay: false		 Invert axis direction (e.g. rankings, depth) or toggle axis visibility for clean sparklines. Bar, Line, Scatter
Zero Baseline beginAtZero: true Ensure linear quantitative axes start at 0, preventing truncated baselines. Bar, Line, Scatter
Grid Controls grid: false
xGrid: true / yGrid: false		 Granularly enable or disable grid lines globally or independently per axis. Bar, Line, Scatter
Area Shading & Fill Opacity area: true / fill: true
fillOpacity: 0.35 / transparency: 0.2		 Turn line charts into shaded area charts with customizable fill opacity. Line
Data Values & Filtering showLabels: true / dataLabels: true
labelFilter: ["Target", "Peak"]
fontSize: 11		 Display direct numeric values, with support for selective label filtering and custom text size. Bar, Line, Scatter
Colors & Fills color: / fill: "#3b82f6"
colors: [...] / palette: [...]
colorScheme: / scheme: "tableau10" / "accent" / "set2" / "turbo"		 Customize palette with hex colors, array lists, or standard D3 categorical schemes. All Chart Types
Legend legend: true / legend: false Toggle legend display (automatically defaults based on series count or categorical/continuous color channel). All Chart Types
Title, Subtitle & Caption title: "Chart Title"
subtitle: "Additional context"
caption: "Figure 1. Source reference"		 Add informative chart titles, subtitles, and explanatory captions. All Chart Types
Container Width width: 80% / width: 600px / width: 500 Sets maximum container width for responsive presentation. All Chart Types
Scatter Trendlines trending: true
trendline: { stroke: "#6366f1", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "4,4", grouped: true }		 Add linear regression trendlines. Supports log-space regression on logarithmic axes, custom styles, and per-series grouping (grouped: true / bySeries: true). Scatter
Scatter Fill & Bubble Size fill: <column> / color: <column>
r: <column|number> / size: <column|number>
colorScale: log / colorLog: true		 Map columns to point fill colors (continuous ramp or discrete swatches) and bubble radii for 4D scatter bubble charts. Scatter
Sankey Links & Flows links: / flows: / series: [{ data: [...] }]
Tuple: [source, value, target] or [source, target, value]
Object: { source, target, value }		 Configure multi-stage flow networks. Nodes are automatically derived or defined via nodes: [{ name }]. Supports custom node/link colors via colorFrom:, colorTo:, colors:, colorMode:, and custom vertical ordering via priority:. Sankey
Schema Mappings schemas: / schema: / mapping:
{ x, y, labels, series, fill, r }		 Map specific table or dataset columns to chart visual dimensions. All Chart Types
Transposition layout: rows / transpose: true Transpose markdown table rows into series and column headers into X-axis categories. Bar, Line
Adaptive Axis Ticks ticks: 6 / x: { ticks: 8, tickRotate: -45 }
y: { ticks: 5, tickFormat: "~s" }
tickRotate: -30 / tickSpacing: 40		 Automatically adapts tick density, stepping, and rotation to prevent label overlapping on dense or narrow axes. Supports explicit tick counts, custom rotation, spacing, and formatting. Bar, Line, Scatter

Examples

1. Bar Chart (with Markdown Table Binding, Transposition & Mark Line)

|  | Test1 | Test2 | Test3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data1 | 1 | 2 | 3.33 |
| Data2 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Data3 | 4.5 | 4 | 2 |

^table-metrics

```chart
type: bar
id: table-metrics
layout: rows
x: "Metrics"
y: "Score"
showLabels: true
markLines:
  - y: 3.0
    label: "Target Benchmark"
    style: dashed
    color: "#f59e0b"
width: 80%
```

2. Line Chart (with Log Scale, Mark Lines & Custom Palette)

```chart
type: line
x: "Quarter"
y: "Revenue ($K)"
yScale: log
showLabels: true
labels: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]
colorScheme: "tableau10"
series:
  - title: "2024 Revenue"
    data: [120, 190, 300, 500]
  - title: "2025 Target"
    data: [150, 230, 340, 580]
markLines:
  - y: 250
    label: "Break-even Milestone"
    style: dotted
    color: "#10b981"
width: 550px
```

2b. Shaded Area Chart (with Area Fill, Opacity & Selective Labels)

```chart
type: line
title: "Monthly Bandwidth Usage"
subtitle: "Network Ingress (GB)"
area: true
fillOpacity: 0.3
beginAtZero: true
dataLabels: ["May", "Jul"]
labels: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul"]
series:
  - title: "Ingress"
    data: [120, 150, 180, 220, 310, 290, 420]
markLines:
  - x: "May"
    label: "Capacity Upgrade"
    style: dashed
    color: "#6366f1"
width: 550px
```

3. Pie, Donut & Polar Area Charts

```chart
type: donut
title: "Document Categories"
labels: ["Markdown Notes", "Web Clips", "PDF Extracts", "Code Snippets"]
colorScheme: "set2"
series:
  - title: "Share"
    data: [45, 25, 18, 12]
width: 320px
```

4. Sankey Flow Diagram (Tuples, Custom Node Colors & Priority)

```chart
type: sankey
title: "Energy Source Distribution"
labels: ["Oil", "Natural Gas", "Coal", "Fossil Fuels", "Electricity", "Energy"]
series:
  - data:
      - ["Oil", 15, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Natural Gas", 20, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Coal", 25, "Fossil Fuels"]
      - ["Coal", 25, "Electricity"]
      - ["Fossil Fuels", 60, "Energy"]
      - ["Electricity", 25, "Energy"]
priority:
  Oil: 1
  Natural Gas: 2
  Coal: 3
  Fossil Fuels: 1
  Electricity: 2
  Energy: 1
colorFrom:
  Oil: "black"
  Coal: "gray"
  "Fossil Fuels": "slategray"
  Electricity: "blue"
  Energy: "orange"
colorTo:
  Oil: "black"
  Coal: "gray"
  "Fossil Fuels": "slategray"
  Electricity: "blue"
  Energy: "orange"
width: 650px
```

5. Radar Chart

```chart
type: radar
title: "Model Comparison"
labels: ["Speed", "Reliability", "Comfort", "Safety", "Efficiency"]
series:
  - title: "Model Alpha"
    data: [80, 90, 70, 85, 60]
  - title: "Model Beta"
    data: [60, 70, 90, 95, 80]
width: 450px
```

^table-countries

```chart
type: scatter
id: table-countries
xScale: log
yScale: log
trending: true
fill: Density
r: GDP
x:
  label: "Land Area (km²)"
y:
  label: "Population"
markLines:
  - y: 10000000
    label: "10M Population Threshold"
    style: dashed
    color: "#f59e0b"
  - x: 1000
    label: "1,000 km² Threshold"
    style: dotted
    color: "#10b981"
width: 700px
```

Observable Plot

Use plot or observableplot for rich data visualizations using Observable Plot. You can write JavaScript expressions or declarative configuration options. Markdown tables with IDs (e.g. ^table-countries) are preprocessed into accessible JavaScript identifiers (table_countries):

```plot
Plot.plot({
  title: "Population vs. Land Area from Note Table",
  width: 700,
  height: 380,
  grid: true,
  x: { type: "log", label: "Land Area (km²) →" },
  y: { type: "log", label: "↑ Population" },
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(table_countries, {
      x: "Land area (km2)",
      y: "Population",
      fill: "Density",
      r: 6,
      tip: true
    }),
    Plot.text(table_countries, {
      x: "Land area (km2)",
      y: "Population",
      text: "Location",
      dy: -10,
      fontSize: 10
    })
  ]
})
```

Inline Comment

Use ::cmt[] for interactive comments/popovers.
